etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle French avarie, from Old French avarie, from Old Italian avaria (which is possibly from Arabic عَوَارِيَّة (ʕawāriyya, “damaged goods”), from عَوَار (ʕawār, “fault, blemish, defect, flaw”), from عَوِرَ (ʕawira, “to lose an eye”)) + English suffix -age.

quote.citation: 2013 June 1, “Towards the end of poverty”, in The Economist‎[1], volume 407, number 8838, page 11:
quote.text: But poverty’s scourge is fiercest below $1.25 (the average of the 15 poorest countries’ own poverty lines, measured in 2005 dollars and adjusted for differences in purchasing power): people below that level live lives that are poor, nasty, brutish and short.

definitions.definition: (statistics) Any measure of central tendency, especially any mean, the median, or the mode. [from c. 1735]
(law, marine) Financial loss due to damage to transported goods; compensation for damage or loss. [from 15th c.]

quote.citation: 2008, Filiberto Agusti, Beverley Earle, Richard Schaffer, Filiberto Agusti, Beverley Earle, International Business Law and Its Environment, page 219:
quote.text: Historically, the courts have allowed a general average claim only where the loss occurred as a result of the ship being in immediate peril. […] The court awarded the carrier the general average claim. It noted that “a ship′s master should not be discouraged from taking timely action to avert a disaster,” and need not be in actual peril to claim general average.

definitions.definition: Customs duty or similar charge payable on transported goods.
Proportional or equitable distribution of financial expense.
(sports) An indication of a player's ability calculated from his scoring record, etc.
(not comparable) Constituting or relating to the average.
Neither very good nor very bad; rated somewhere in the middle of all others in the same category.

quote.citation: 2002, Andy Turnbull, The Synthetic Beast: When Corporations Come to Life, page 12:
quote.text: We tend to think that exceptionally attractive men and women are outstanding but the fact is that they are more average than most.

quote.citation: 2004, Deirdre V. Lovecky, Different Minds: Gifted Children with AD/HD, Asperger Syndrome, and Other Learning Deficits, page 75:
quote.text: Things that never would occur to more average children, with and without AD/HD, will give these children nightmares.

quote.citation: 2009, Susan T. Fiske, Social Beings: Core Motives in Social Psychology, page 73:
quote.text: In other words, highly attractive people like highly attractive communicators and more average people like more average communicators.

definitions.definition: (informal) Not outstanding, not good, banal; bad or poor.

quote.citation: 2002, Andy Slaven, Video Game Bible, 1985-2002, page 228:
quote.text: The graphics, sound, and most everything else are all very average. However, the main thing that brings this game down are the controls - they feel very clumsy and awkward at times.

quote.citation: 2005, Brad Knight, Laci Peterson: The Whole Story: Laci, Scott, and Amber's Deadly Love Triangle, page 308:
quote.text: But what the vast majority of the populace doesn′t realise is the fact that he′s only on TV because he became famous from one case, Winona Ryder's, which, by the way, he lost because he′s only a very average attorney.

quote.citation: 2009, Carn Tiernan, On the Back of the Other Side, page 62:
quote.text: In the piano stool there was a stack of music, mostly sentimental ballads intended to be sung by people with very average voices accompanied by not very competent pianists.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To compute the average of, especially the arithmetic mean.
(transitive) Over a period of time or across members of a population, to have or generate a mean value of.

quote.citation: 1961 November, “Talking of Trains: The roller-bearing A1s”, in Trains Illustrated, page 643:
quote.text: The five roller-bearing A1s are now averaging 120,000 miles between shopping; this figure is an improvement of about 50 per cent on the norm of other ex-L.N.E. Pacific types.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To divide among a number, according to a given proportion.
(intransitive) To be, generally or on average.

quote.citation: 1872, Elliott Coues, Key to North American Birds:
quote.text: Gulls average much larger than terns, with stouter build  […]

etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English average, from Medieval Latin averagium, from aver (“horse or other beast of burden, service required from the same”) from Old English eafor (“obligation to carry goods and convey messages for one's lord”) from aferian (“to remove, take away”); + -age.

definitions.definition: (UK, law, obsolete) The service that a tenant owed his lord, to be done by the animals of the tenant, such as the transportation of wheat, turf, etc.
